title: Drift Wood #28 · the Rain, ii
logline: January again. Wood tries to explain rain to Gully. Gully explains it back.

panels.composition: The boat launch in January. Rain so hard it's a texture. GULLY under the shack's eave with a thermos. WOOD beside him, pad under his coat.

characters.pose: beside him, pad hidden under coat

balloons.text: Ozu would have held this shot for two minutes. No cut. Just rain.

image.prompt: two teenagers sheltering under a shingle shack's eave at a boat launch in torrential January rain drawn as dense vertical hatching, one holding a thermos, black and white

balloons.text: A Japanese director who understood that nothing happening is something happening.

image.prompt: close-up of a boy in a backwards cap drinking from a thermos under an eave in the rain

balloons.text: Rain's not nothing. Rain's the river coming up and the crab coming in and the road going out at milepost six.

image.prompt: a boy in a backwards cap nodding out at heavy rain from under an eave, a thermos in his hand

panels.composition: Silent. The rain, held. Two minutes. No cut.

image.prompt: a silent wide panel of torrential rain over a boat launch and a dissolving bay, two small figures under a shack's eave, dense vertical hatching, black and white, no words

notes: The second Rain. Gully's definition is the strip's, from here on.
